details:
There's a thousand and one people, who will justifiably explain where you could've done better but I would like to ask for a change to the root cause of the issue. 

The Vrchat Dev team didn't communicate well, at all, and almost never has. Let's change that. 

The problem, at it's core, is that it looks like you do. But talking to people on twitter, discord, canny, etc, isn't good enough. Talking alone, isn't good enough. You have to do it right.

Let's go over where and how things should be different and how you could've done EAC better, from a communication standpoint. 

• You should've put out an official update, through steam, twitter, and everywhere, that you were thinking of putting in EAC. You should do for this all major changes. And especially, put the announcement into the actual game menu itself. You know, where you are suppose to put important information in the giant header. Now you might think you did this but no, this was not a discussion, this was an announcement of a removal of a bunch of features. That's not the same thing as discussing something. You should make discussions of major changes an integral part of development, before you just decide to add or remove stuff. You should announce it via the ways mentioned above.  

• You should have weekly twitches, about an hour long, discussing the progress of vrchat. It doesn't have to be in detail, it doesn't have to be specific, but it should exist, just so we all know how things are going. We all could have learned that you were working on and cared about malicious mods and were running into problems with development because of mods *long* before this all happened and you would have received heaps of ideas on how to go about things. Instead, let's roughly say, you had a problem (malicious and regular mods making everything hard), you spent (let's be generous) 3 months planning, deciding, and getting EAC. That's 12 weeks you could've gotten help from the community to fix issues, if we had just known. There's better anti-cheats out there alone, let alone other changes and ideas everyone could've had. You didn't let the community help you at all.

• You knew the QoL mods were going to be a massive issue. They are core features to your game, even if you don't recognize them. What you are doing, is equivalent to removing every feature you've added in the last 3 years. Vrc mods are not "other." They are an equal part, if not more so, than your own development.   Altogether, all the mods have probably done more development on your game than you have. They've definitely added more features. Way, way more features. You should've communicated that you were specifically working on officially adding those (something you haven't even done now.) How long is it going to take? Are you going to do it at all? We need more than vague words vrc devs. We need "yeah we are working on adding these 12 specific things and it'll take take us probably between 14 and 18 months." You should've had this ready and out, long before considering EAC. Because, to reiterate, you are removing features from the game. That is the essence of what you've done. The least you can do, is tell people when you are going to give them those features back. The least. You did this once (the twich dev stream roadmap) and things changed and that's fine. You can't make everyone happy and no one likes to hear guilds still aren't here or half a dozen other stuff we expected but that's a natural part of development. You can't make everyone happy but you can communicate and thus prevent people from getting as angry. If it changes, change the roadmap of progress, keep it more vague, give reasons, but don't just not do it like you have been so far. We need more roadmaps.

That's the core essence of the request I have. Announce discussions before making decisions on stuff, do weekly twitch streams an hour long of progress, and let us see your roadmap of whats being worked on and where things are at and talk to us about your problems. 

You've made a lot of people angry and let's be clear, that was always going to happen.  Even if you did things, a lot, better, you were probably going to add some anti-cheat and it was probably going to remove mods. But the level of anger is because you communicate what's going on poorly or not at all and that gives everyone the feeling that you don't listen. Really think on this next part I say, if any dev reads this:

Some of these mods, are what made your game playable for some people, and you announced via complete surprise, that they can essentially no longer play your game until you add them back. That could be years. That's not an exaggeration. That's literal.

What part of that is good communication? That's not rhetorical or passive aggressive, like it might sound. It's a real question. You decided to do things this way, instead of any other way. Literally, I am asking any dev that reads this, what parts of that were good communication and what were bad? How could you do things better? Please, think about that.  

Vrchat is a social game and the community is more than willing to help you guys, if you'd let us. 

To reiterate my feature request: Better announcements, twitch streams, roadmaps, and overall, better communication.
title: Better communication, especially after EAC
